subject: Inference dimensioning + token bandwidth proposal for HelionAI - next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marc Dwyer <marc@helion.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Inference dimensioning + token bandwidth proposal for HelionAI - draft attached

Marc — attaching the initial dimensioning we discussed on Friday. Summary up top:

- Baseline workload: 120k daily active end users, average request = 140 tokens in, 220 tokens out (response), estimated 50k total requests/day.
- Target SLOs: 95th latency <= 220ms for short chat (<= 128 tokens), 95th <= 700ms for long context (<= 1024 tokens).
- Expected steady-state token rate (tokens/sec sustained): ~1800 tps. Peak 5-min burst expected up to 6k tps (based on marketing campaign + morning peak).
- Recommended Dedicated footprint: 4 x A100-80GB equivalent for baseline sustained load with 40% headroom; add 2x A100 as burst buffer (auto-burst policy).

Attachments: helion_token_bandwidth_model.xlsx (token-to-gpu mapping + per-endpoint profiles), sla_fit_matrix.pdf (SLO fit summary).

Key asks: can you confirm the expected QPS distribution across short vs. long prompts (sheet "traffic_profile") and whether Helion is comfortable with auto-burst for up to 2x reserved (we can set conservative cost controls)?

If that sounds right, Jonas can produce the per-GPU p95 latency curves and a few pricing scenarios for committed vs. burst.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — this looks like the right direction. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Traffic profile: current split is ~70% short prompts (<=128 tokens) and ~30% long-context (>=512 tokens), but marketing push next month could shift short prompts to 80% for short bursts.
2) Can you confirm expected cold-start behavior? We have long-running KV caches on our side; want to understand warmup token penalties.
3) For procurement: procurement@helion.ai will need an itemized commitment quote (monthly reserved + burst allowance).

Can Jonas and Marissa loop in any runtime constraints you see? I'd like a short paragraph we can share with finance explaining expected monthly committed spend and burst surcharge % so procurement has a starting point.

—Marc

Subject: Re: Inference dimensioning + token bandwidth proposal for HelionAI - draft attached

Marc — quick technical addendum based on Soojin's workbook and the profile you provided. High-level calculations (rounded):

- Short prompts (70% assumed): 35k requests/day -> avg tokens/sec steady from shorts = 70 tps.
- Long prompts (30%): 15k requests/day -> avg tokens/sec steady from longs = 1730 tps.
- Combined steady-state ~1800 tps (matches Soojin's sheet). Peak (marketing short bursts): short-heavy burst could push total to ~6000 tps for 5-10 minutes.

GPU mapping (A100-80GB equated):
- For short prompts (low seq length) we can achieve ~600 tokens/sec per GPU (conservative, with batching).
- For long-context workloads with KV cache warmed, effective throughput per GPU ~450 tokens/sec due to KV ops and attention memory.

Sizing recommendation:
- Sustained cover: 4 GPUs (4 * 450 = 1800 tps). That matches sustained load.
- Headroom: +40% recommended for OTA/unknown variability -> 6 GPUs (sustained + headroom = 2520 tps).
- Burst buffer: Add 2 ephemeral GPUs (or burst to shared pool) to hit 6000 tps five-minute peaks if combined with autoscaling and prefix cache warms.

Latency fit notes:
- With current model quantization and batching settings, short prompt p95 ~180-210ms on a single GPU under expected concurrency; long-context p95 ~500-650ms depending on batch. We can tighten p95 by reducing batching at cost of efficiency (token price).

Operational risks and mitigations:
- Cold KV warmup: first request latency penalty ~+250-400ms for long contexts; recommended pre-warm strategy for scheduled campaigns.
- Concurrency cliffs: avoid large global batch windows during peak marketing pushes; recommend dynamic batch caps per route.

I'll attach a quick per-GPU p95 curve chart to the Drive link and can export two pricing scenarios: (A) committed 6-GPU slab with 2-GPU burst allowance, (B) committed 4-GPU with aggressive burst and queue shaping.

Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Inference dimensioning + token bandwidth proposal for HelionAI - draft attached

Marc — from a commercial/ops perspective I'd propose the following next step sequence so procurement has exactly what they need:

1) Quote doc (itemized): monthly committed units (6 GPU-slab), burst allowance (2 GPUs, billed per-minute overage), and estimated token price under standard quantized profile.
2) Runbook: short playbook for campaign warmup (pre-warm jobs, KV shadowing) and rollback triggers.
3) SLA summary: p95 commitments per route and fallback policy (fallback to smaller-latency model variant if SLO approaches breach).

I can draft the quote template this afternoon if you confirm preferred commitment term (6 months vs 12 months). Shorter term -> higher per-GPU rate but more flexibility.

Also tagging the attachments we expect to include: helion_token_bandwidth_model.xlsx, sla_fit_matrix.pdf, and the draft quote PDF.

Marissa
